claim: At d_model=64, the seed-24 N=128 run (m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, e<=0.5, 6000 steps) has trained force R2 0.70465 at its best-margin layer 3. That is 0.080 below the d_model=128 value of 0.78436, but the d128 value is at layer 1, so this is a cross-layer comparison. Force only barely beats its control (0.59931, margin 0.105 vs required 0.1, persistent from step 4500; headroom-normalised 0.26). accel_step does far better: R2 0.93863 at layer 4 vs control 0.71496 (margin 0.224, normalised 0.79, formed at step 500). The paired d_model=64 N=64 seed-24 arm is not in the provided results, so the N=64 minus N=128 gap was not computed.
confidence_note: The first condition holds: N=128 force R2 is 0.70465, below the 0.765 cutoff and well outside 0.01 of d128. That points to N=128 force rising with width, as seed 23 did (0.696 to 0.765 to 0.788). Four things limit confidence. (1) The decisive test, a d64 gap of at least 0.077 against at most 0.068, needs the paired d64 N=64 seed-24 run, which was not available. The verdict therefore cannot be supported or refuted. (2) The width comparison is cross-layer: d64 layer 3 vs d128 layer 1. probes_final gives no layer-1 force value for this run, so a same-layer gap cannot be computed. The best-margin layer also wandered between 2 and 3 over training. (3) This is one seed, one run, and one data_seed, with seeds_agree false. (4) The force margin is 0.105 against a 0.1 bar, though control_spread is small (0.003). The verdict would become supported if the paired d64 N=64 run gives a gap of at least 0.077, ideally confirmed at layer 1 in both arms. It would become refuted if that gap is at most 0.068, or if layer-1 N=128 force at d64 is within 0.01 of 0.78436.
